clue.text: Drivers tucked into fresh motel porridge

indicators.note: something tucked into a thing is placed inside it, so one set of letters goes within the other
a fresh version is a new one, so the letters are made over in a new order

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, the British motoring organisation for drivers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Motorists staying at a newly done-up motel are served porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The two As go inside the letters of motel, and the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Oatmeal is ground oats, and the porridge made from it is also called oatmeal, especially in America.

clue.text: With nothing to mark award?

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
a scar is a mark left on the skin

explanation.surface: A wry question whether an award is earned just for leaving no mark at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oscar is the popular name for the Academy Award statuette given for film achievement.

clue.text: Return to market place escaping, opening crush

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a mart is a market
PL is the standard abbreviation for place in street names

indicators.note: an opening is the start of something, so only the first letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of escaping

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing back to a crowded market square is caught in the opening crush.
explanation.walkthrough: "Market place" reads as one phrase but splits into two pieces, and "opening crush" also splits: the indicator belongs to escaping, leaving crush as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trample is to tread something down heavily, flattening or crushing it underfoot.

clue.text: Style shown by some private landlords

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are shown, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: found running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A comment on the flair displayed by certain private landlords.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is dash or flair, a stylish vigour in how something is done.

clue.text: Relax when London weather is unsettled

indicators.note: unsettled things are thrown out of order, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Londoners can finally unwind when the changeable weather settles, or perhaps when it does not.
explanation.definitionFit: To let one's hair down is an idiom for dropping formality and enjoying oneself freely.

clue.text: Drink alcohol for comfort

parts.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone takes a drink to console themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Support as a noun means comfort or encouragement given to someone in difficulty.

clue.text: Frank expression clearly winning round student

parts.note: straight means plainly or directly, without ambiguity

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: taking a prize is winning it
L is a learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A frank remark about a student who is the obvious winner.
explanation.walkthrough: "Clearly winning" suggests a straight win, but the two words give separate pieces; the learner goes inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight talking is honest, direct speech that says exactly what is meant.

clue.text: Stay to have a look at reported information

parts.note: a stay is a support or prop

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the spelling follows how the phrase sounds

parts.note: to have a gander at something is British slang for having a look at it

explanation.surface: Someone stays on to read some reported information.
explanation.walkthrough: A gander is informal British for a look; said in a non-rhotic accent it ends like the last part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is information, often biased, spread to promote a cause or point of view.

clue.text: Unlikely to be away with the team

parts.note: someone away is out
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A player is unlikely to travel with the squad for an away game.
explanation.definitionFit: Outside describes a slim possibility, as in an outside chance of winning.

clue.text: Old news

parts.note: surface reading: stale reports everyone already knows; setter's reading: an old-fashioned word for news

explanation.walkthrough: Old news usually means something stale; here old describes the word itself, which is archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidings is a literary, old-fashioned term for news or announcements, as in glad tidings.

clue.text: Letter about current agreement

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a charter is a formal agreement or grant of rights
AC is alternating current

explanation.surface: A letter concerning a current agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The outer word splits after its fourth letter to take the two-letter current.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a single written symbol, such as a letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Decided to change depot

indicators.note: to change something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A firm made up its mind to switch to a different depot.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose, so having opted means having made a decision.

clue.text: Ready with rent rebate at last

parts.note: a rip is a rent or tear

indicators.note: at last points to the final position, so only the end letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of rebate

explanation.surface: A tenant is all set now that the rent rebate has finally come through.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid to a landlord, but here it is a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is ripe is ready to eat, and a plan that is ripe is ready to act on.

clue.text: In a manner of speaking, without a clue

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: diction is one's style of enunciation
taken as written

explanation.surface: A comment that someone, so to speak, has no idea.
explanation.walkthrough: "Without a clue" reads as clueless, but without means outside and clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An indication is a sign or hint pointing towards something, which is what a clue provides.

clue.text: Sheer power might be shown by animal

parts.note: a brute is a beast or animal
might and force both mean strength

explanation.surface: Raw strength is what you might see from a wild beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Might looks like a verb ('might be'), but it is the noun for strength; the animal piece comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brute force is raw strength used without skill or subtlety.

clue.text: Remains with newcomer and retired teacher

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman newly introduced to society

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn or gone back, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: Something is left behind by a new arrival and a retired schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is the scattered remains of something broken or destroyed.

clue.text: Exclamation comes out of the blue!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: A sudden cry bursts out unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: "Out of the blue" reads as the idiom for unexpectedly, but the blue is the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The heavens are the sky, and the plural is also an interjection expressing surprise.

clue.text: One has to retain extraordinary stillness

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their usual order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone must keep up an unusual degree of calm.
explanation.walkthrough: Retain looks like the verb in the sentence, but it is the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a lack of motion or activity, a tendency to remain still.

clue.text: Refusal to conclude this is hellish

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for a noun: the answer is the hellish thing

parts.note: to infer is to conclude from evidence
no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Declining to end things is described as torture.
explanation.walkthrough: "Refusal to conclude" reads as a refusal to end, but the refusal simply follows the verb for drawing a conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: An inferno is a raging fire, and Dante's Inferno is Hell itself, so it is a hellish place.

clue.text: Chose to miss start of exclusive by journalist

indicators.note: missing the start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: select means exclusive, open only to a few
ED is short for editor, the crossword's stock journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter decided to pass up the first part of an exclusive story.
explanation.definitionFit: Elected is the past tense of elect, meaning picked or chose by preference or vote.

clue.text: Glances saucily away from game when drunk

indicators.note: taking something away from a word removes those letters from it

parts.note: tiddlywinks is a game of flicking small discs into a cup
a wink is a cheeky, flirtatious glance

explanation.surface: Someone stops making eyes across the room once they have had a few.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiddly is British informal for slightly drunk or tipsy.

clue.text: Allow to look through brochure

parts.note: to leaf through a book is to look through it
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Permission to browse a brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: The allowing word is attached to the end of the looking word.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a small printed sheet or folded pamphlet of information, much like a brochure.

clue.text: General discussion of liberal floral arrangement

parts.note: liberal and free both mean unrestricted

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People talk at length about a lavish display of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: "Floral arrangement" reads as a bunch of flowers; here the arrangement acts on the word floral.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is an open discussion or fight in which anyone may join in.

clue.text: The actors are shy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the performers in a play
second meaning: a throw, as in a coconut shy

explanation.surface: The performers are bashful.
explanation.walkthrough: Shy looks like an adjective, but it is the verb or noun for a throw.
explanation.definitionFit: The cast is the company of actors in a production, and to cast is to throw, as is to shy.

clue.text: Subject: not us (fourth-rate)

parts.note: them is the other side as opposed to us
E is a fourth-grade mark after A, B, C and D

explanation.surface: A snooty note that some topic is beneath us and decidedly inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the subject or topic of a talk, piece of writing or work of art.

clue.text: Big names turn up with shady character

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up flips the letters to read from the bottom

parts.note: VIPs are very important people

explanation.surface: Celebrities arrive accompanied by a dodgy dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: A spiv is British slang for a flashy petty crook dealing in black-market goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a small-time wheeler-dealer living on shady deals, hence a shady character.

clue.text: Deterioration of worn central engine part

parts.note: rot is decay

indicators.note: central points to the middle, so only the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of worn

explanation.surface: A worn-out central engine component has deteriorated.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine such as an engine, turbine or helicopter.

clue.text: Spontaneously smile upon stumbling

indicators.note: stumbling is tripping out of step, so the letters fall out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grins without thinking after tripping over.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on impulse means acting suddenly without planning.

clue.text: Affectionate address by veteran runner

parts.note: a veteran is old
the runner bean is a climbing bean

explanation.surface: A warm greeting from an experienced athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: Runner reads as an athlete, but it is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Old bean is dated British slang used to address a friend warmly, like old chap.

clue.text: Dance performed with exaggerated content

indicators.note: content is what a thing holds, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: to give a show is to perform it
OTT is over the top

explanation.surface: A dance was put on with over-the-top flourishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The gavotte is an old French dance of moderate tempo.
